title: Sequences, attention and transformers
summary: Sequence information boundaries, scaled attention, masks, permutation symmetry, positions, multihead costs and a decoder audit.

objectives.description: Compute scaled dot-product attention with shapes, masks and stable normalisation.
Distinguish conditional linearity in values from full input-dependent attention.
Prove unmasked permutation equivariance and understand positional/causal structure.
Calculate attention parameter/memory costs and audit sequence-prediction leakage.

preparation.description: Read queries/keys/values, multihead and transformer components, positional encoding and training. Videos are optional and were not used as verification.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Self-attention is a fixed linear map of its inputs.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It is linear in values only when attention weights are held fixed; those weights generally depend on inputs.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A zero masked score excludes a future token.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It contributes exp(0)=1; exclusion must occur before normalisation.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A causal mask repairs same-position target leakage.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Inputs and next-token targets must also be shifted correctly; the current input can otherwise reveal the answer.
